vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.4

The skill bundle contains standard documentation (SKILL.md) and metadata (_meta.json) for a Gmail reply functionality using an external 'gws' CLI tool. There is no executable code, obfuscation, or evidence of malicious intent; the instructions are consistent with the stated purpose of managing email replies and attachments.

llm.summary: The skill itself is a thin wrapper that calls the gws CLI (which fits the described purpose), but it hides authentication/credential requirements in an external shared SKILL.md that is not declared here — that mismatch warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (reply via Gmail) align with the runtime instructions (invoke gws gmail +reply). Requiring the gws binary is expected. However, the skill points to a ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth and global flags but does not declare any required environment variables or credentials itself — a potential omission/mismatch.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only documents the gws CLI usage, which stays on-purpose, but it explicitly tells the agent to read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth/security rules and to run gws generate-skills if missing. That delegates critical auth behavior to another document (not visible here) and potentially to generated files. This delegation expands scope and hides where credentials/configuration are actually read or written.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no bundled code — lowest risk. It merely requires the gws binary to be present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no environment variables or primary credential, yet it defers to gws-shared for auth. That suggests required credentials (OAuth tokens, API keys, local config files) may exist but are not declared here, which is a proportionality/visibility problem — users cannot see what secrets this skill will need without inspecting gws-shared.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there is no install writing code or modifying other skills in this package. The only persistence hint is gws generate-skills (which may create files), but that behavior is invoked only if the user runs it; it is not forced by this skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill simply runs the gws CLI to send threaded Gmail replies, which matches its description — but it defers authentication and security rules to ../gws-shared/SKILL.md. Before installing or enabling this skill, inspect the referenced gws-shared SKILL.md (or the output of gws generate-skills) to see exactly which credentials, config files, or tokens are used and where they are stored. Verify the provenance and trustworthiness of the gws binary (it will have full mailbox send/reply capability). Consider: 1) what credentials (OAuth client secrets, refresh tokens, service account keys) are required and whether you’re comfortable granting them; 2) whether gws generate-skills will write files or tokens to disk and where; and 3) whether you want the agent to be allowed to invoke this skill autonomously (agent autonomy can result in emails being sent without further prompts). If you cannot inspect gws-shared or confirm credential usage, treat the skill as higher-risk and avoid installing it.
